$comment: CONSOLIDATED INDEX — hands-on competitor capture round 1. GENERATED by scanning the capture files in this directory; never hand-written. Every entry resolves to a file here. If this index and a capture file disagree, the capture file wins.
status: NO COMPETITOR IS COMPLETE. All 17 touched; none exhausted. See ROUND-LEARNINGS.md 'Owed'.

findings.claim: Priority support — the benefit a low-confidence traveller needs most — is gated behind 15 completed bookings in 2 years, so it is structurally unreachable by a first-time traveller.
The Genius programme never addresses a first-time traveller anywhere on its own explainer page.
The market leader contractually disclaims liability for the exact failure experience a reassurance-led product would want to own — at least for flights.
Booking.com does operate a disruption mechanism, but only where it holds the supplier relationship.
Accessibility is a contractual term, not only a design commitment — section A11 'Accessibility requests' sits in the Terms of Service.
The statement names no accessibility standard and makes no conformance claim.
Accessibility of the actual travel experience is routed away from Booking.com to the supplier.
Across three first-party documents Booking.com consistently occupies an intermediary position and pushes responsibility outward at every layer.
Booking.com offers no ranking axis based on effort, ease, stress or traveller confidence. Every axis is price, a quality proxy, distance, property type, or an opaque default.
Booking.com DOES disclose that commercial terms affect ranking — so a blanket claim that competitors never explain their recommendations does not hold here.
Loyalty membership changes the ranking surface by exactly one axis, and that axis is another PRICE axis.
Booking.com fires a Google One Tap sign-in prompt at a signed-out user during search.
The primary Reserve control is inert until a room quantity is selected, and nothing states this.
No account is required to reach the booking form. There is no sign-in wall and no guest-checkout prompt either — the question is simply never asked.
Booking.com's answer to multi-type trip attachment is three opt-in checkboxes inside the booking form.
Expedia carries six verticals to Booking.com's four booking types, adding Packages and Cruises — but presents a far smaller link surface on the homepage.
Romie — named in prior desk research as the most serious competitive threat and the top open question — does not appear anywhere on the Expedia homepage.
see capture file
Both loyalty programmes examined so far gate their better rates behind accumulated bookings, and neither addresses a first-time traveller anywhere on its own explainer page.
For an identical city and date range, Expedia returns 499 properties where Booking.com returns 4,194 — roughly an eightfold difference.
Expedia offers no ranking axis based on effort, ease, stress or confidence. Enumerated positively from the opened control.
Expedia collapses guest details and payment onto ONE page; Booking.com splits them across two, with no payment field present on its details step.
Expedia's insurance decline option is written as a confession of recklessness rather than a neutral choice.
Google Travel exposes four decision-support surfaces that neither Booking.com nor Expedia offers anywhere in their accommodation journey.
Google Travel hands off rather than sells. No 'Book on Google' surface was present on the accommodation result.
Google Travel offers three ranking axes: an opaque default, price, and a quality proxy. None concerns effort, ease, stress or confidence.
The product with the richest decision-support layer has the poorest ranking layer.
Google Travel is the only product observed that tells a traveller what a normal price looks like before they search.
Authentication unlocks exactly one capability on Google Travel, and it is a functional one — persistent price monitoring — not a discount.
Two products, two matched-pair diffs, one extra capability each — but of opposite kinds.
Google Flights publishes an explicit all-in pricing commitment — the stated opposite of drip pricing.
Google Flights explicitly addresses a traveller who has not decided, in its own copy.
see capture file
Google Flights states its ranking criteria in plain language on the result set itself.
On a live route, Google states whether the current price is normal and when to buy — without requiring a booking, an account, or a commitment.
Google Flights surfaces a comparison dimension that is neither price, quality proxy, nor distance: carbon emissions, expressed relative to the route average.

Across 20 enumerated ranking axes on three products, ZERO concern effort, ease, stress or confidence. This was described as the load-bearing finding of the round and the basis of Luma's differentiation.
Emissions is a selectable sort axis, not merely a displayed attribute. F-34's OWED test is settled.
Kayak ships a standalone Flight Tracker at /tracker — a direct analogue of a named Luma core feature.
The ad-landing variant renders the same product surface as the clean URL. The tracking parameters produced no observable difference.
see capture file
Kayak places an 'IA' (AI) entry point directly beside its wordmark in the primary header.
Kayak's AI planner ships a designed empty state. This is the first empty state observed anywhere in the round across four competitors.
Kayak's travel AI accepts photo and file upload as planning input, not just text.
The planner asserts the traveller's location unprompted, and asserted it incorrectly.
Kayak's sort control displays the consequence of each choice on the control itself — price AND duration on every tab — so the trade-off is legible before the user commits to a sort.
Two of Kayak's three flight sort axes concern duration, confirming that effort IS ranked in flights on a second product.
Kayak labels paid placements explicitly and in the first person of the advertiser.
From a flight result set, Kayak asks whether the traveller wants bus prices.
Two meta-search products state opposite pricing commitments for the same product category.
Kayak sells combined itineraries assembled from separate airlines, each governed by its own conditions, with no single carrier owning the journey.
Kayak's handoff on this result went directly to the airline that operates the flight, not to a reseller.
Within a single Kayak result set, the protection a traveller ends up with varies enormously — and nothing in the ranking, sorting or price display reflects that.
Crossing the handoff, the traveller loses all trace of the product that sent them and immediately faces a fresh consent gate.
Booking.com, Kayak and Rentalcars.com — competitors 1, 4 and 9 on the roster — are all Booking Holdings companies. Verified from first-party statements on two of the three.
Kayak publishes an 18,759-character document explaining how it recommends content and orders results, broken down per vertical.
Three competitors, one browser session, one afternoon — and each asserts a different location for the same traveller.
Skyscanner offers search with no destination at all — 'Explora cualquier lugar'.
Skyscanner's own FAQ headings directly address the confusion the handoff creates.
Hopper ships a family of flexibility products, not a single one.
Hopper's web surface permits search but gates its differentiating products behind the app.
AirCover is included in every accommodation booking at no cost. It is the opposite commercial model to Hopper's Premium Disruption Assistance, for the same category of promise.
Airbnb states what AirCover is NOT, in plain language, with concrete examples — inside the same document that sells the reassurance.

findings.confidence: Verified as a description of the two products' stated scopes. The consequence is Inferred — no traveller was observed in this state.
findings.claim: Placed together, Airbnb and Hopper cover opposite halves of the journey and neither covers the seam.
Airbnb offers no sort control at all. It is the only competitor observed with none.
Airbnb displays the total price for the stay and never a nightly rate. Every other accommodation competitor observed leads with a nightly figure.
see capture file
Airbnb offers travel insurance at checkout with a neutral, priced question. Expedia phrases the same decision as a confession of recklessness.
Airbnb offers three payment timings, one of which defers the entire cost at no additional charge.
Airbnb states whether the price is normal, at the moment of payment.
Airbnb gives the traveller no way to reorder results and the most detailed explanation of its ordering found anywhere in the round.
Airbnb states that its algorithm deliberately favours variety — showing different hosts, characteristics and price points rather than the single best-scoring set.

findings.confidence: Verified as an observation about the DOCUMENT.
findings.claim: The five stated factors contain no commission, advertising or paid-placement term.
Airbnb holds stays, experiences and services under one account and still does not model the trip as a single object. Moving from an accommodation search to experiences drops the trip entirely.
Airbnb shows accommodation as a total for the stay and experiences as a price per traveller. The same product uses two conventions in two verticals.
Tripadvisor's primary entry point is a question rather than a search field label.
'Descubrir' (Discover) is a top-level navigation item, alongside 'Opinión' (Review).
Tripadvisor's primary verticals are things to do, hotels and restaurants. No flights vertical was present on the homepage.

Two extraction sweeps on this page returned TRAVELLER REVIEW TEXT. A 'filterGroups' selector aimed at headings pulled review titles, and a 'cancellationSignals' regex pulled a complaint about a failed booking modification.
Tripadvisor surfaces activity duration — but only inside seller-written titles, never as a structured, comparable field.
Tripadvisor states the basis of its rankings on the results surface.

findings.confidence: Verified — first-party statement on the product's own homepage.
findings.claim: Rentalcars.com states on its own homepage that it is part of Booking Holdings — the same parent as Booking.com, competitor 1.

findings.confidence: Verified that the CLAIM is made. NOT verified that it holds — no booking flow was walked, and car hire is the vertical where counter-desk charges, fuel policy, insurance excess and deposits classically appear after the headline price.
findings.claim: Rentalcars makes an explicit no-hidden-charges claim on the homepage.
The cancellation promise carries a qualifier that most travellers will not weigh.
Trainline offers to notify the traveller when they QUALIFY FOR DELAY COMPENSATION — not merely when a delay occurs.
Trainline's search form carries a PRE-CHECKED Booking.com Genius cross-sell which, on search, opened a Booking.com hotel search in the original tab — with dates that are not the travel dates.
Trainline surfaces duration and change-count per result and offers a 'Direct only' filter.
Trainline states its ranking basis and leads with two effort criteria before price.
A search for Madrid to Barcelona could not be completed. A cookie consent modal — 'Administrar preferencias de cookies' — intercepted the input and blocked the search form.
Omio's consent modal states it shares personal data with 164 partners.
Omio accepts city, station, airport OR port in a single origin field and compares across four transport modes in one result set.
Omio ships an AI planner as a primary tab beside the standard search — 'Planificador IA'.
Rome2Rio presents duration and price together, per transport mode, in one view — including modes no other roster competitor surfaces.

findings.confidence: Verified for the rendered surface; the load caveat applies.
findings.claim: Rome2Rio surfaces no booking or purchase language on the comparison view — consistent with the roster's assumption that it routes and compares without fulfilling.
Citymapper presents transit options with frequency, calories and cross-mode alternatives alongside price and duration — three attributes absent from every other competitor in the roster.
Across the roster, effort is now observed measured in three different units, and which unit is used depends entirely on what the vertical can compute.
TripIt models the trip as one object — and does so by ingesting other products' confirmations, without selling anything.
TripIt's organisation is free; the features that address traveller anxiety are behind TripIt Pro.
TripIt sells pre-trip entry-requirement guidance as a named Pro feature.
The meta-search handoff deposits the traveller, pre-selected, into the airline's most restrictive fare family.
Iberia states an all-in total with a named exception. Kayak, which sent the traveller here, states that its prices exclude baggage fees.
Iberia's airport services are bundled with Business class, not sold as add-ons. The page title scopes them to a fare class in its own words.

findings.confidence: Verified as an observation about Iberia; the market inference is Inferred, from this single capture.
findings.claim: Business goal 5 assumes airport services are a purchasable product. On the first supplier examined they are a fare-class entitlement, which changes who Luma would be selling to.
Iberia ships a chat assistant, 'Ibot', present on this page.
Iberia explicitly distinguishes voluntary changes from operational disruption, states that the traveller's rights are different, and then provides no route to them.

findings.confidence: Verified — each link in the chain is an individually verified capture in this round.
findings.claim: Traced end to end, the traveller's protection degrades at every hop and is never displayed at any of them.
Iberia Club is the only loyalty programme of the three examined whose currency can be earned without travelling at all.
Iberia Club extends programme benefits to children as a stated feature.
Three loyalty programmes, three full-page text searches, zero mentions of a first-time traveller.
American Airlines publishes a Customer Service Plan containing explicitly named disruption sections.

I ran the symmetric findability sweep on AA using ENGLISH terms — delay, cancel, disrupt, compensat, rights, irregular, service plan, refund — against a page served in SPANISH. It returned zero matches for every category including loyalty and lounges, which should have been the tell.
aa.com redirects to americanairlines.es for a Spanish-locale session, serving a materially thinner site — 43 links against a US site that hosts a full Customer Service Plan.
AA's Spanish homepage surfaces travel disruption prominently — as a heading, not a buried link.

findings.confidence: Verified that these products exist as named destinations. Their mechanics and prices were NOT captured.
findings.claim: Qatar Airways sells the loyalty currency, the STATUS points, and a paid subscription to the loyalty programme itself.

findings.confidence: Verified that these destinations exist. Whether any is PURCHASABLE by an economy passenger was NOT determined — no pricing page was opened.
findings.claim: Qatar Airways treats the airport as a destination with its own product line, unlike Iberia where airport services are a Business-class entitlement.
No disruption, delay, cancellation, compensation or passenger-rights destination appears in Qatar Airways' 289 homepage links.

findings.confidence: Verified that both facts hold. The INFERENCE that one can buy enough Qpoints to reach Silver is Inferred — purchase limits and whether bought Qpoints count toward tier qualification were NOT captured, and many programmes explicitly exclude purchased points from tier progression.
findings.claim: Lounge access sits at Silver — the first tier above entry — and Qpoints, the currency that reaches Silver, are sold by Qatar Airways.
Privilege Club runs three distinct currencies.
Four loyalty programmes, four full-text searches, zero mentions of a first-time traveller.

findings.confidence: Verified for the mechanism and the unit price. UNKNOWN for the caps.
findings.claim: F-108 inferred that lounge access is indirectly purchasable, because lounge access sits at Silver and Qpoints are sold — but flagged that many programmes exclude PURCHASED points from tier qualification, and that the inference was unverified.
Qatar Airways publishes a unit price for loyalty status: USD 25 per Qpoint.
